data.one_liner: Open iOS and Android phone settings pages from a Flutter app.
data.what_it_does: A Flutter plugin that provides methods to open specific device settings pages, such as Wi-Fi, location, volume, and general application settings, on Android and iOS.
use_when: You need to direct users to specific system settings pages from within your app.
You want to open Android Q+ settings panels for quick configuration changes.
avoid_when: You only need to launch general URLs or web pages.
You need to directly modify system settings without user navigation.
strengths: Supports multiple platform settings types including location, Wi-Fi, and volume panels.
Dependency-free core package with optional AI proposals via a companion package.
Supports Swift Package Manager for iOS integration.
weaknesses: Settings panels are limited to Android Q and higher.
Unsupported settings types fallback to general application settings.
data.setup_notes: For iOS using Objective-C, add use_frameworks! to your Runner project Podfile. Swift Package Manager is also supported.

alternatives.name: url_launcher
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you primarily need to open standard URLs, phone calls, or emails rather than specific OS settings pages.

alternatives.name: permission_handler
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need to handle permissions and request user access instead of just navigating to the settings screen.

data.minimal_example:
ElevatedButton(
  onPressed: () => AppSettings.openAppSettings(type: AppSettingsType.location),
  child: const Text('Open Location Settings'),
)
